Maria: Heads-up — Nimbus just pinged Sales for final commit sizing. They want a firm monthly GPU-hour commit + a small buffer for holiday traffic. Can we sketch numbers?
Sanjay: Quick context: customer's current peak steady-state is ~320 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day. They asked for 20% buffer initially.
Ellie: Us-west-2 inventory note: we only have ~120 A100-equivalent GPUs free for Q4 after internal reservations. APAC reserved surge drops available burst by ~30% during their November promo.
Andrew: Cost calc quick take: at our Dedicated pricing, 1 A100-eq GPU-hour ≈ $3.8 blended; 320*24*30 ≈ 230k GPU-hours/month -> ~$870k/mo. Buffer adds materially.
Jules: If we accept 20% buffer that's ~276k GPU-hours/mo. That's above their target commit tier, would push them into a higher reserved slab. Could propose a 15% buffer + 10% burst credit.
PMLaura: From Sales: Nimbus is willing to sign a 12-month commit if latency SLOs hold and we include predictable burst policy. They pushed back on penalties for under-provisioning.
Sanjay: Proposal we discussed internally: base commit = measured 90th percentile usage (210k GPU-hrs/mo), buffer = +15% (242k), plus a transient burst allowance = 10k GPU-hrs/mo (billed separately). That keeps price near their target but gives runway.
Ellie: Two constraints: 1) region capacity (us-west-2) — can't sustain 10k extra burst continuously in November. 2) networking: their cross-AZ bandwidth requirement spikes with multi-replica serving, need to reserve extra vNIC throughput, which we should quantify.
Maria: Can someone run a quick availability check & simulated schedule so we can confirm we can meet 95th pct latency at that commit + buffer?
OpsBot: inventory-check finished: us-west-2 projected free A100-eq GPUs by month - Oct: 110, Nov: 85, Dec: 95. (trigger: inventory-check --region=us-west-2 --horizon=3mo)
Andrew: That inventory means our proposed burst of 10k GPU-hrs in Nov likely impossible without rebalancing other Dedicated customers or moving Nimbus workloads to a secondary region. Cost to reassign ~ $15k one-time migration ops + small weekly uplift.
Jules: Option B: offer cross-region failover — primary us-west-2 commit, overflow routed to us-east-1 at same rate but with a 5% traffic steering fee. Keeps latency within SLO for most requests, some tail penalty for geo-sensitive traffic.
Sanjay: For contract language, recommend: 1) 12mo commit at 242k GPU-hrs/mo (15% buffer), 2) documented burst pool up to 10k GPU-hrs billed at on-demand rate, 3) automatic region fallback with explicit APAC/geo exceptions.
PMLaura: Sales OK with that if we include an SLA clause for region fallback and a playbook for failback. Also they want a 30-day ramp in usage so we can stagger capacity handover.
Ellie: Action items: I can run a placement plan and network throughput calc — need confirmation of expected peak RPS and average sequence length from Sales.
Maria: I'll loop in Solutions Eng to get the workload profile. Also please prepare two pricing lines (with and without burst credit) for legal.
Andrew: I'll draft the cost impact note for Finance, include expected uplift if we reassign capacities.
Jules: I'll draft the contract buffer language and the fallback playbook (short checklist).
Sanjay: If we can't free up enough us-west-2 capacity, we should be explicit with Nimbus: either reduce buffer to 10% or accept cross-region overflow.
Maria: Thanks — sync at 11am to finalize numbers. cc @PMLaura @Ellie @Jules :thumbsup:
